E. CFO action table: what should have been done (2020-26) - evidence is live
What the CFO should have done
D/E (all debt) rose 0.53x (FY20) to 1.95x (FY26); cover fell 13.7x to 6.8x
Set an explicit guardrail (cover >= 6x, D/E <= 1.5x) and fund the post-2022 inventory build with equity-like cash flow and longer-tenor debt, not rolling commercial paper.
Short-term share of borrowings 99% in FY26; +250 bp costs Rs 385 cr (cover 5.2x)
Term out at least 40-50% of borrowings and swap about 75% to fixed before the 2022 cycle; the hedged column in section B shows the saving.
Gold on loan funds 38% of inventory in FY26 (peak 50%)
Raise gold-on-loan to about 45% of inventory: it is a natural hedge with the cheapest funding; avoid net-open gold positions as prices spike.
Hedging reduces cost of financial distress
Payout 24%-36%; FCF after dividends negative in 3 of 6 years
Keep the smoothed policy (it signalled stability) but link DPS growth to FCF after working capital; do not raise DPS faster than EPS when FCF is negative.
No buy-back at 20x+ book. If cash is surplus, special dividend or deleveraging beats repurchase.
Capex/dep 0.39x in FY21 and 0.56x in FY22, then 1.09x
Protect core capex through shocks (it fell 59% in FY21 and recovered); fund store and factory capacity before the cycle turns, since ROIC > WACC in 5 of 6 years.
Cash / borrowings 0.37x in FY26 vs 3.1x in FY22
Hold a liquidity buffer of at least 20 days of revenue or committed lines equal to 50% of short-term borrowings.
